chunks: From him, from his father, from Ibn Abī ʿUmayr, from Ḥammād, from al-Ḥalabī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

For the muwaddiḥah there are five camels; for the simḥāq there are four camels; for the bāḍiʿah there are three camels; for the maʾmūmah there are thirty-three camels; and for the munaqqilah there are fifteen camels.

key_terms.ٱلسِّمْحَاقِ: a wound reaching the thin membrane over the bone
key_terms.ٱلْإِبِلِ: camels, the unit used here for legal compensation
key_terms.ٱلْبَاضِعَةِ: a wound that cuts into the flesh
key_terms.ٱلْمَأْمُومَةِ: a wound reaching the membrane of the brain
key_terms.ٱلْمُنَقِّلَةِ: a wound that displaces or moves the bone
key_terms.ٱلْمُوضِحَةِ: a wound that exposes the bone

ai.seo_question: What are the prescribed diyah amounts for different types of head wounds in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith states fixed compensatory amounts for specific categories of head and facial injuries. It is part of the legal rulings on diyāt, detailing the prescribed indemnity measured in camels for each type of wound.
